# Layers Glossary

## Terms

This glossary lists software design layers, separation of concerns, modular boundaries, framework independence, adapter terminology, and common words used in architecture conversations. It exists so a team can align on names such as domain layer, application layer, infrastructure edge, policy, orchestration, and interface boundary without debating the same phrases repeatedly.

## Naming Guidance

The note is intentionally reference-oriented. It explains how people label layered structures, what a boundary usually means in conversation, and which synonyms appear in architecture reviews. It may mention runtime, transport, storage, policy, or adapters as vocabulary anchors, but it does not teach the concrete execution flow that keeps business rules isolated from outer tools.

## Reference Scope

Use this note when the task is to clarify wording, compare terms, or document a shared glossary. Do not use it as the primary runtime guide for deciding how requests cross the application boundary or where policy should stay during execution.
